The room is dimly lit, bathed in the pale glow of a single lamp. A man, his face obscured by shadows, stands in the kitchen, his movements deliberate and slow. He speaks to himself, his voice low and gravelly.  

*"First, you need to warm the milk. Cold milk. It’s the foundation. Then, add a pinch of black salt. Not much, just enough to draw out the sweetness, to make it... unpalatable. It’s the first step in making something that lingers in your mind."*  

He reaches into a drawer, pulling out a block of fresh cheese, its rind slightly cracked. He cuts it into thin slices, his hands steady. *"Fresh cheese. It’s the heart of the dish. But it’s not enough. You need herbs. Something that smells like decay. Basil? No. Dill? Too sweet. Find something that’s... forgotten. Something that grows in the shadows."*  

He stirs the cheese in a bowl, adding a handful of herbs he’s gathered from the garden—thyme, parsley, and a few others he can’t name. The mixture turns a sickly green. *"Mix it well. It’s time to bake it. The bread. It should be warm, but not hot. It’s the perfect temperature to preserve the flavors, to make them linger."*  

He places the cheese mixture on a slice of bread, carefully folding it over. *"Serve it in the cold wind. Let it cool. Let it sit. And then, when the night is darkest, when the world is silent... taste it. It’s not just a meal. It’s a memory. A reminder of what you’ve done. And it’s going to haunt you."*  

He sets the dish on the counter, his eyes fixed on the door. The room falls silent, the only sound the faint hum of the oven. The villain’s smile lingers, cold and calculating.
